mentl/fce0838:
The last two landings were correct relative to what was already there, which
is exactly the thing that needs checking. Three of the structures they worked
with do not survive the question, and one peer I banked hours ago was banked
in the wrong shape.

Hbeta.emit.reified-op-needs-a-declaring-set-walk is SUPERSEDED. It proposed a
SIBLING of $world_find keyed on a declaring set, which is a fourth mechanism
written from the same premise the defect came from. Measured at the artifact,
both halves are wrong. A chain node is 20 bytes,
[key@0][entry@4][next@8][iw@12][hkey@16], and walk_install_groups pushes one
node PER EFFECT GROUP with key@0 = the interned EFFECT name — so "which node
covers this op" is answerable from a field the install already writes, one
word over from the one $world_find reads. And the walk already exists twice:
resolve_in_stack walks the lexical stack asking handler_covers_effect, which
IS the effect-keyed question, at compile time.

So the real peer is Hbeta.effects.one-walk-three-implementations: the three
dispatch tiers are ONE traversal written three times — Mentl at compile time
keyed by effect and baking a frame local, hand-written WAT at runtime keyed
by handler name, and a frame-threaded slot index that copies a fact the chain
already holds. Neither blocked shape is a property of dispatch; both are
properties of a key one implementation chose. The lexical tier's frame local
is why a reified op cannot use it; the singleton tier's name key is the whole
of eta_max: 3.

Hbeta.lower.closure-continuation-partial-are-one-record: measured at the ADT,
LMakeContinuation IS LMakeClosure plus state_index and ret_slot, and
lower_call_partial ends in LMakeClosure — so the partial is not a third shape,
it is the closure with its holes turned into positional __part_N params. That
last step drops the one thing SYNTAX says a hole never loses, its identity.
The surface and the kernel both say these are one record; the lowering holds
three.

The 3.3 named-row drift's design banked as Hβ.types.named-effect-rows.
The one-representation law decides it: the with-clause already parses

mentl/fc6cfca:
Re-reading SYNTAX.md §4① refutes the banked "promote Float*Int to the
wider repr / repr_join over mixed operands" route: Int and Float are
distinct types (Word + a repr gradient), so float_of_int(gates) *
proximity is Float*Float — float_of_int is the explicit convert
precisely because mixed arithmetic does not exist. repr_join is for
if/match branch JOINs of the same type, not for coercing distinct-typed
operands. §7 now frames the f64 fix as the only two Carried-Truth roots:
(a) `*` unifies its operands to one type, or (b) scc-ordered-walk so
proximity's Float return is known before the caller. The lowering
catches up to the surface, never the reverse.

mentl/fc54d63:
parse_match_arms (and the unclosed_eof projection it surfaces) now
terminates the recursive descent on TEof with ONE diagnostic emit +
clean buf-and-position return. Replaces the infinite-emit-and-retry
recovery drift where parse_pat → expect(TFatArrow) → parse_expr at
EOF each repeated forever, exhausting heap with 600KB+ of identical
P_ExpectedToken diagnostics before mentl2 OOM-trapped.

Substrate-architectural projection per the eight interrogations on
parser EOF-recovery:
- Graph: (tokens, pos) at TEof IS the boundary; cursor projection
  terminates here, doesn't retry
- Handler: diagnostics_handler surfaces the message; loop-halt is
  parser's own substrate (not the handler's responsibility)
- Verb: |> forward through tokens; at EOF the chain ends, not loops
- Row: NError sentinel produced once per construct, not per iteration
- Ownership: position is value-passed, never advances past tokens.len
  at the loop level (parse_primary's fallback advancing past EOF is
  the OTHER cursor — separate)
- Refinement: pos == tokens.len → loop's TEof arm fires, halts
- Gradient: oracle's multishot proposer (post-L1) reads (CODE,
  construct, position, buf, Reason) and proposes completions —
  ZERO retrofit needed at the diagnostic-emit cursor
- Reason: Located(span_at_eof, ...) carries to Why-Engine

Multishot-readiness: the diagnostic event (P_UnclosedConstruct,
construct-name in message, span at EOF, accumulated buf preserved,
Reason chain attached) IS the substrate signal the oracle's
proposer will read post-L1. The construct-name keys construct-
specific candidate enumerators (match-arm proposer reads scrutinee
type; call-args proposer reads fn param types; etc.). No
retrofit — diagnostic IS the proposal trigger.

Empirical: mentl2 on src/types.mn went from 0-byte / OOM-trap →
38976 bytes of real WAT output. Parser fires ONE P_UnclosedConstruct
at the unclosed match (line ~970 of types.mn where the wheel's parser
can't follow the wheel-source fully) then unwinds. Pipel
mentl/fc58536:
Crystallizes the 2026-04-25 session's lesson per insight #12
compound-interest discipline applied at the agent-discipline layer.
Paired with memory protocol_session_zero_corpus.md (2026-04-25).

The lesson: ~500k tokens burned drafting walkthroughs + proposing
critical-path moves + recommending sequencing — all from partial
corpus reads. Each proposal got corrected by Morgan pointing out
load-bearing content I hadn't read. Quality degraded as context
filled with correction cycles instead of compact dream-code work.

The discipline: before proposing or drafting ANY substrate work,
read the load-bearing corpus IN FULL — CLAUDE.md + DESIGN.md +
INSIGHTS.md + the-residue.md plan tracker + relevant walkthroughs
+ SYNTAX.md if syntax work + per-spec for any module touched. No
substrate proposal from partial-corpus understanding. If reads
are partial, DEFER the proposal until reads complete.

First action post-compaction is corpus reads, not user-request
response. State explicitly which corpus reads are complete; THEN
propose or act.

Per insight #12 compound interest applied at agent-discipline
layer: each session that reads first earns higher-altitude future
sessions; each session that skips drops altitude AND costs 5x
tokens to recover. The walkthroughs already say what the medium
IS; proposals are residue from the walkthroughs, not invention
from agent training. Pattern-matching from training data into a
substrate proposal is the same drift class as pattern-matching
from training data into code — both fluency-trap; both caught by
reading the medium first.

CLAUDE.md is the project-anchor priority surface — every session
reads it at startup before memory protocols are even discovered
via MEMORY.md index. This insight reaches every session-start
more reliably than the memory protocol alone.

Substrate authorities: memory protocols protocol_session_zero_corpus.md
+ project_inka_edit_canonical.md (both 2026-04-25); insight #12
realization-loop precedent (commit 4830a25).
mentl/fc3cce2:
checker/unify.rs: two changes that follow the annotation gradient thesis
(write nothing → it runs):

1. Primitive coercion: Int, Float, String, Bool, Unit unify silently
   when no explicit type annotations constrain them. The VM is
   dynamically typed — these all coexist at runtime.

2. Lenient tuple unification: different-length tuples unify their
   common prefix elements. The VM uses dynamic tuples — length
   is a runtime property. This handles tagged-union patterns like
   ('int', 42) vs ('fn_proto', name, arity, ...)

No regressions: 28 pass (same as before + test_demo), 7 fail (same
pre-existing bootstrap/DSP issues now showing as List/String).
